TESTIMONY OF THE
DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND
WILDLIFE
IN SUPPORT OF L.D. 47
"An Act to Provide an Exception to a Fishing Prohibition near the Crooked Brook Dam."
SPONSORED BY: Representative Mason of Lisbon
DATE OF HEARING: February 3, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Liz Latti, Fisheries and Hatcheries Director at the
Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, speaking on behalf of the Department, in support of L.D. 47, An Act to Provide an Exception to a Fishing Prohibition near the Crooked Brook Dam.
Construction of a new fishway has recently been completed at the Crooked Brook dam in Danforth. In conjunction with the project, the Town of Danforth is developing a new community park and gathering space adjacent to the new fishway. This location has
historically been a popular fishing spot for town residents.
With the completion of the fishway, due to the prohibition within Title 12, Section 12457 the area within 150-feet of an operational fishway is closed to fishing and
therefore would restrict fishing at the new community park in Danforth.
This bill was brought forth by the department and it makes an exception to the 150-foot
fishing setback around the Crooked Brook Dam fishway which allows fishing closer to
the fishway but still prohibits fishing in or from the fishway for safety reasons. This bill proposal will allow continued historical fishing opportunities, particularly for local youth
who frequent the site to fish due to its convenient access and location.
This bill would also align Crooked Brook Dam fishway with the other 10 exceptions of
the prohibition of fishing in or from the fishway in the state. The Department has coordinated with the town of Danforth and the Department of Marine Resources on this proposal and they are both in support. I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.

TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF:

LD 47, "An Act to Provide an Exception to a Fishing Prohibition near the Crooked Brook Dam."

THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE

SPONSORED BY: Representative Mason of Lisbon
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and fellow distinguished members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Representative Rick Mason representing part
of Lisbon and I am here today to introduce my bill LD 47, "An Act to Provide an Exception to a Fishing Prohibition near the Crooked Brook Dam. "
The Crooked Brook dam in Danforth has historically been a popular fishing spot for town
residents. Fishways are closed for fishing within 150-feet due to a prohibition within Title 12,
Section 12457. With the completion of the new fishway and the development of a new community park, the historical fishing opportunities provided to this community should
continue.
This bill was brought forth by the department and it makes an exception to the 150-foot fishing
setback around the Crooked Brook Dam fishway which allows fishing closer to the fishway but
still prohibits fishing in or from the fishway for safety reasons. This bill also aligns with the other 10 exceptions of the prohibition of fishing in or from the fishway throughout the state.
I would now like to defer to Liz Latti, Fisheries and Hatcheries Director at the Department of
Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to provide answers to your questions and explain it more in depth
concerning this department-initiated bill.
